messages.subject: težave s Tinn-R-om?
messages.body_plain:
Nekateri poročajo, da imajo težave z nastavitvijo Tinn-R-a. Simptom je najpogostejši ta, da se Rterm oz Rgui iz Tinn-R-a ne zažene, oz. da se nastavitve ne ohranijo in se ob ponovnem zagonu Tinn-R-a resetirajo.

Ker so strici, ki so odgovorni za razvoj R-a v zadnji verziji spremenili strukturo direktorijev, Tinn-R tega sam ne zna zaznati. Zato mu moramo to dopovedati mi. To storimo tako, da v opcijah nastavimo pravilno pot do datotek Rterm.exe in Rgui.exe (Options > Application > R > Path, nato pa klikneš "Search path" za vsako datoteko). Da se bodo nastavitve shranile tudi ob ponovnem zagonu programa pa na vprašanje "Use latest installed version (always)?" odgovorite z No. Da bo bolj jasno prilagam sliko. Hvala Mojci H., da je priskrbela posnetke programa.

lp,
Roman

--

messages.subject: opomnik - 2. R delavnica
messages.body_plain:
Pozdravljeni!

Rad bi vas spomnil na 2. delavnico za novince v okolju R, ki bo v
sredo, 10. 11. 2010 ob 16. uri na Oddelku za biologijo. Predavalnico
bomo določili glede na obiskanost delavnice, vsekakor ste znova lepo
vabljeni, da s seboj prinesete svoje prenosne računalnike. Ker smo
porodne krče 1. delavnice prestali, bo šlo tokrat vse malce hitreje,
zato vas še enkrat vabim, da poskusite rešiti domače naloge in ponovno
preberete tistih nekaj vrstic transkriptov prejšnjega srečanja, ki smo
vam jih že poslali.

Iz njih je razvidna tudi tema 2. delavnice: delo z objekti tipa
data.frame. Naučili se bomo uporabljati kup funkcij, s katerimi se
lahko lotite svojih podatkov, ter seveda uvoziti podatke iz
razpredelnice tipa Excel v R. Nekaj nalog, ki že uporabljajo nekatere
"nove" funkcije, najdete spodaj - spopad z njimi vam bo gotovo
poenostavil sredino delavnico.

Skratka, prav lepo vabljeni!

Luka

#
*********************************************************************
# 2. delavnca - naloge
#
*********************************************************************

# Ustvari matriko m, ki bo vsebovala 999 naključnih števil iz
# normalne porazdelitve (?rnorm), razvrščene v 3 stolpce. Izračunaj
# povprečja vrednosti po stolpcih z uporabo funkcije mean() in
# z indeksiranjem (oglati oklepaji) matrike.

# Povprečja stolpcev lahko enostavno izračunate tudi s funkcijo
colMeans().
# Funkcija vam vrne povprečja v obliki vektorja. Pripnite vektor "na
dno
# matrike" - torej kot 334. vrstico - z uporabo funkcije rbind().
# Na analogen način izračunajte povprečja vrstic s funkcijo rowMeans()
in
# jih dodajte matriki z cbind().

# Pretvorite dobljeno matriko v data.frame df (funkcija
data.frame()).
# Dodajte stolpcem imena "prvi", "drugi", "tretji", "povprecje"
# (funkcija names()). Imena vrstic(row.names()) pa naj bodo
# c(1:333, "povprecje").

# Iz df (data.frame iz prejšnje naloge) naredite dva manjša data.frame-
a:
# df1 naj vsebuje 1. in 2. stolpec vrstic 1:100 , df2 pa vrstice
101:200 s podatki
# iz 2. in 3. stolpca. Z uporabo indeksiranja (oglati oklepaji)
preverite, ali:
#	- je element v 5. vrstici 2. stolpca v df1 večji od 0?
# 	- je vsota elementov 3.vrstice v df2 večja od 5?
#	- je povprečje 1. stolpca df1 večje od povprečja 2. stolpca df2?
#	- kakšno je ime 2. stolpca v df?
#	- itd., dokler suvereno ne obvladate oglatih oklepajev.

messages.body_plain:
Anka,
po mojem bi ti rada imela vec grafov na isti sliki, to je v istem oknu (ki se mu po domace baje rece graphic device). Najpreprosteje je uporabiti lattice paket, kot je omenil Roman - ta peket zna narisati vec grafov skupaj z eno vrstico kode, tako da podatke recimo združuje po kakem kljucu itd. Priporocam, da si pogledaš kake primere, recimo vtipkaj:

library(lattice)
example(xyplot)

Skupaj s slikami boš dobila tudi kodo, ki ti bo morda pomagala pri prvih korakih s tem paketom.

Ce pa že znaš narisati boxplot z istoimensko funkcijo in bi rada samo vec takih slikc na istem oknu, lahko poskusiš tudi tako, da spremeniš graficni parameter, recimo:

par(mfrow=c(2,2))

Ta ukaz bo povzrocil, da bo graphic device pricakoval od tebe 4 grafe in jih bo organiziral v dva stolpca in dve vrstici (številke po potrebi spremeni, jasno). Za tem ukazom 4x zaženi boxplot() z želenimi parametri (lahko v zanki) in ti jih bo narisal v isto okno/na isto sliko.

Upam, da ti to kaj pomaga. Sicer vprašaj! Pa še namig: grafika (risanje grafov, vizualizacija podatkov) bo tema 3. delavnice v sredo, 24.11. Vabljeni!

LP
 Luka

V primeru, ko imam prevec slik za hkratno prikazovanje (vec sto), jih shranim na disk in jih nato preklikam s pregledovalnikom slik. Ko se odlocim, katere so uporabne, se jim posebej posvetim. Ce uporabiš R za avtomatsko generiranje slik, jih je enostavno pridelati zelo veliko - vse, kar stane, je le procesorska moc - pregledaš pa jih nato v nekaj minutah. Glede na opisano torej ti želiš delati natancno to, veliko slik pa pridelaš tako, da se prezankaš skozi podatke (torej ne vtipkaš ukaza za vsako sliko posebej). Zato svetujem, da v kodo daš nekaj takega:

count = 0   #nek števec si omisliš (pred zanko)
...         #zanka - manipulacija podatkov itd.
  jpeg(paste("imeMojeSlike",count,".jpg", sep=""))   #sliko naj shrani v .jpg fajl, števec sliki zagotavlja unikatno ime
  boxplot(.....)     #tvoj ukaz, kako naj nariše sliko
  dev.off()          #zapreš graphic device
  count <- count+1    #povecaš števec za 1 (da bodo vse slike imele unikatno ime!)

Na ta nacin ti bo slike spravil v delovno mapo (getwd()), kjer jih lahko nato pregledaš in ovrednotiš.

V tretje gre rado - upam, da ti ta rešitev ustreza.

LP
 Luka

messages.body_plain:
Dear Dragan,

1. You did not define the factor with which you want to compare with in the sample set.

          SampleID Time Frequency Amplitude
1            a                1          x               y
2            a                2          x               y
3            a                3          x               y
4            a                4          x               y
5            a                5          x               y
6            b                1          x               y
7            b                2          x               y
8            b                3          x               y
9            b                4          x               y

2. I do not get completely your aim of the comparison. Do you want to compare dominant frequency (the frequency with the highest amplitude), average ampitude, or something else? In sound analysis the former is mostly used. Than we can ask the question whether you want to compare for instance dominant frequencies and its amplitude between samples (A) or amplitude on different selected frequencies between samples (B). In method B you have a selected number of frequencies which you want to measure the amplitude. This can be useful when you already know the frequency distribution and where the frequencies with the higher amplitudes are. When you would only do three cross sections like described in method B it is possible that you miss the highest frequency. It might be therefore be better to ask yourself the question whether there are differences in dominant frequency between the samples. For this you will need more rectangles (one rectangle would be an influx of frequency (it is not really clear what the sound sample is and what the influxes of frequency stand for)) randomly chosen within one sample. Optimal is more than 30 but 10 is also ok.  However, this also increases to chance for statistical difference, which make biological no sense. Be aware that sample closer in time are more similar than later in time. This creates dependency among eachother. Measurements sampled in time can be more independent when there is a larger time gap in between. I don't know how large this should be for bees.

When you got the data which is needed, you have to check whether the response variables (frequency and amplitude) are normally distributed per sample. This you can check with a histogram. If this is the case you can use an ANOVA if not you can (log or square root) transform the data and hope it will be normally distributed and do an ANOVA. If this is not the case, you can use the non parametric Kruskal wallis test, which can also compare differences between more samples, but is more robust than the ANOVA. After that you will know that there is a difference between the samples, but not where is the difference. For this you can use a post hoc test. For the ANOVA you can use the Tukey test (TukeyHSD(ANOVA output))and with the Kruskal Wallis test there is a post hoc test in the package "pgirmess".

If you have more questions or remarks please let me know. If you like we can discuss this eye to eye, I will this afternoon at the R course otherwise we can meet in biološko središče on another time of the day.

Kind regards,

Maarten

Ne vem, če je že kdo to omenil... enostavna in po moje najbolj uporabna rešitev je, da klikneš "recording" grafov (ko si v grafičnem oknu, klikni v GUI-u history>recording). Potem lahko s PgUp in PgDn gledaš grafe, ki si jih že zrisala.

Drugače pa lahko odpreš več grafičnih device-ov (kar si najprej spraševala).

windows()
- odpre novo grafično okno in ga nastavi za aktivnega.

Potem pa imaš celo serijo dev.nekaj ukazov

dev.next, dev.cur, dev.prev....

Če recimo hočeš nastavit naslednje okno za aktivno, napišeš dev.set(dev.next())

Poglej:

?windows
?dev.cur

Kot izhodni device lahko nastaviš tudi disk, kot je nakazal že Luka. Pogosto zelo elegantna rešitev, če proizvajaš veliko slik/grafov. Poglej ?win.metafile

Drugače je jpeg precej slab format za grafe, ker je lossy (razen pri zelo nizki kompresiji naredi "packe" ob črtah) - namenjen je prvenstveno fotografijam. Običajno se vektorski formati precej bolje obnesejo (wmf, pdf), od rastrskih pa je png kar zakon.

Hi Maarten,

seems you really know your way around statistical analysis of data.

It also looks like that my initial email lacks to define what my question actually is, like Roman mentioned.

The reason may very well be that I did not really know how to ask the question but fortunately your answeres have some of the key vocabulary that I can use to describe my issue.

1.
The key for sure is to find out how amplitude changes with regards to frequency - I agree that most useful frequency to be used for this is dominant frequency, but will this be enough? I think I should use more freqencies, if this will give me more complete picture of  sound analysis than only comparing dominant frequency? Will it? As I discused this with my mentor at the time we were recording he also did not want to limit comparing of results solely on dominant frequency.

2.
But since I want to compare how bee sound amplitudes change with regards to relevant frequencies while bees are exposed to different factors (alcohol, insecticides, wheather...) I must assume that dominant frequency will not always be the same, so from this point of view rectangle data that does not relate to single frequency might be better?

Your second paragraph is really heavy - you really know how to do statistical analysis. Since you mention we can meet eye to eye I would gladly accept this since writing this stuff is really something else than discussing it eye to eye. I did visit Rkoholiki group meetings last year but I work in Novo mesto and your R meetings begin while I am still working so it is quite difficult for me to attend your classes. Can we meet after R course on wednesday - I am not sure if I will make it on time for the R course, but I can defenatelly be there until it is over. I can make necessary arrangements at work so you can propose any other day and time, whatever is ok for you.

Kind regards,

Dragan

> Dear Dragan,
>
> 1. You did not define the factor with which you want to compare with in the sample set.
>
>           SampleID Time Frequency Amplitude
> 1            a                1          x               y
> 2            a                2          x               y
> 3            a                3          x               y
> 4            a                4          x               y
> 5            a                5          x               y
> 6            b                1          x               y
> 7            b                2          x               y
> 8            b                3          x               y
> 9            b                4          x               y
>
> 2. I do not get completely your aim of the comparison. Do you want to compare dominant frequency (the frequency with the highest amplitude), average ampitude, or something else? In sound analysis the former is mostly used. Than we can ask the question whether you want to compare for instance dominant frequencies and its amplitude between samples (A) or amplitude on different selected frequencies between samples (B). In method B you have a selected number of frequencies which you want to measure the amplitude. This can be useful when you already know the frequency distribution and where the frequencies with the higher amplitudes are. When you would only do three cross sections like described in method B it is possible that you miss the highest frequency. It might be therefore be better to ask yourself the question whether there are differences in dominant frequency between the samples. For this you will need more rectangles (one rectangle would be an influx of frequency (it is not really clear what the sound sample is and what the influxes of frequency stand for)) randomly chosen within one sample. Optimal is more than 30 but 10 is also ok.  However, this also increases to chance for statistical difference, which make biological no sense. Be aware that sample closer in time are more similar than later in time. This creates dependency among eachother. Measurements sampled in time can be more independent when there is a larger time gap in between. I don't know how large this should be for bees.
>
> When you got the data which is needed, you have to check whether the response variables (frequency and amplitude) are normally distributed per sample. This you can check with a histogram. If this is the case you can use an ANOVA if not you can (log or square root) transform the data and hope it will be normally distributed and do an ANOVA. If this is not the case, you can use the non parametric Kruskal wallis test, which can also compare differences between more samples, but is more robust than the ANOVA. After that you will know that there is a difference between the samples, but not where is the difference. For this you can use a post hoc test. For the ANOVA you can use the Tukey test (TukeyHSD(ANOVA output))and with the Kruskal Wallis test there is a post hoc test in the package "pgirmess".
>
> If you have more questions or remarks please let me know. If you like we can discuss this eye to eye, I will this afternoon at the R course otherwise we can meet in biološko središče on another time of the day.
>

messages.subject: directory & startup
messages.body_plain:
Dear R gang,

I have 2 questions:

1. I find it impossible to to set permanent source folder from which my data would be uploaded into R. If you use R/file/change dir... the source folder is set only for current R session. But I want the same folder to be already set whenever R is started. It can be done since I used this feature in the past, but my computer broke and after new R installation I just couldn't remember how I did it the first time.

2. How do I make R automatically load certain packages at start, so I do not need to upload it manually every time it is started. Once I alredy managed to do it by modifying Rprofile.site file (use command ?Startup for instructions) but just couldn't do it again after my computer broke.

It would be nice if somebody who knows how to do it to, just correct this Rprofile.site file content for me:

Kind regards,

Dragan

messages.body_plain:
In my experience, using specific folder for each little project worked out best. Every project gets its own script file. To accommodate the correct working directory for calling files, I use setwd() at the start of every script. This is the method I use to keep my folders and files tidy.

It seems to me like your Rprofile.site is incomplete (or is this just a clip?). In any case, this post <https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-help/2004-January/044701.html> should give you a general idea of how to proceed.

Bad experience has led me to become advocate against the saving of workspace (you end up chasing a bug that isn't - it's just your bad data that is not what you think it is). This causes havoc if you're rerunning the analysis at a later date. That's why it's wise to have a script for every project and rerun it each time. Of course, you may have analysis that takes too long to do every time, then saving your workspace may be sensible.

Cheers,
Roman

3. Glej 2.

4. Kriva je tista vejica. :) Tabele ni potrebno obračati. Funkcija za plotanje bo pojedla vektor, in ji je vseeno, ali je to vektor iz stolpcev ali vrstic.

lp,
Roman

messages.subject: following session: data exploration
messages.body_plain:
Dear Rkoholiki,

Tomorrow will be the next session about R. This time it will be about
the start of analysing your data. Before testing hypotheses on your data
set, you first have to explore your data in order to make any decision
which test you will need to use. During this session I will give tools
and tips to explore your data set. For the eager once among you, you can
already read a bit in the article of Zuur et al 2009, "A protocol for
data exploration to avoid common statistical problems"
(http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.2041-210X.2009.00001.x/pdf) (free
down-loadable). Furthermore, I would ask you to download already the
"car" library and the "AED" library. The latter library can be
downloaded and installed from the following link:
http://highstat.com/Book2/AED_1.0.zip. Please also take your own data
set of for instance your student work, diploma or doctoral thesis or
work with you so you can straight away apply the new learned tips and
tools. If you don't have these we will provide another data set for you.
I think that also people who are not yet comfortable with coding in R
will also be able to understand course material.

Kind regards,

Maarten
